item.title: Declaration of Independence Exhibition Grand Re-Opening — Thu Sep 24, 4:30 PM — Lilly Library
item.description: Presented by Lilly Library Celebrating a Historic Year Open configuration options IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to an opening event on September 24, 2026, celebrating the expansion of our exhibition The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment, newly joined by The Signers in our South Gallery. We welcome IU Associate Professor of History Konstantin Dierks, who will give a lecture entitled “The Declaration in a Time of Crisis.” How do people meet the moment in times of political crisis? The Declaration of Independence tried to meet the crisis of 1776. It pinned blame on King George III. It inspired enough colonists to rebel against a mighty empire. It put enduring ideals into American history. The Declaration managed to do so surrounded by a crisis—and before a future—far beyond its grasp. How might we think, then, of the issues we face in 2026? Professor Dierks’ talk will be followed by a reception with exhibition curators and seasonal refreshments. During this

item.title: Always A Little Bit Tipsy — Thu Sep 24, 7:30 PM — The Waldron Firebay
item.description:
Presented by After the Storm Productions The world premiere of Always a Little Bit Tipsy will take place in Bloomington, Indiana this September! Based on the topsy-turvy life of world-champion ballroom dancer and drag artist Tom Slater (a.k.a. Tipsy Teasedale) the all-new original musical, Always a Little Bit Tipsy, explores survival, masculinity, and the healing power of drag. This is a story about the violence of small shames, the masks we build to survive, and the radical act of becoming whole. Tickets: afterthestorm.ludus.com
Source: WFIU Community Calendar

item.title: Indianapolis Symphony Orchestra – Jun Märkl, music director; Spencer Myer, piano soloist — Thu Sep 24, 7:30 PM — Musical Arts Center
item.description: Repertoire Mussorgsky/Rimsky-Korsakov: Night on Bald Mountain (1867) Beethoven : Piano Concerto No. 4 in G Major, Op. 58 (1806) Stravinsky: The Rite of Spring (1913/48) About the Artists Jun Märkl is a highly respected interpreter of the core German repertory, and has become known for his refined and idiomatic explorations of the French Impressionists. He serves as music director of the Taiwan Philharmonic (National Symphony Orchestra), music director of the Indianapolis Symphony Orchestra, and chief conductor of the Residentie Orkest The Hague, Netherlands. item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Fri Sep 25 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Fri Sep 25 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Fri Sep 25 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Fri Sep 25, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: 2026 Old Town Waverly Park Festival — Sat Sep 26, 12:00 AM
item.description: The annual Old Town Waverly Festival includes demonstrations and reenactments of Backwoodsman, Blacksmithing, weaving, competitions, live music and more. View historical items located in the Waverly Museum which was the Old Town Waverly Bank building or wander and enjoy the antique tractor display and vendor booths. Old Town Waverly Park is a place to re-connect with nature and history. Stop by on Saturday, from 9 am to 6 pm or Sunday, from 10:30 am to 4 pm. 2026 Schedule Ongoing Activities \(both days\): Craft/Art Vendors, Traditional Craft Demonstrations, Food Court Vendors, Historical Encampments, Farm Town, Kids Town, Historic Hayrides, & Riverview Golf Cart Tours. Saturday: 8 -11 am - Community Breakfast, Historical Methodist Church 9:55 am - Muzzleloader salute 10 am - Vendors open, Town Square 10 am - Flag Raising by Boy Scout Troop 231 Patriotic music from Woodbridge Music Academy 10:15 am - Welcome and Celebration of 250 years of our Independence 10:30-11 am - Music by Woodrid

item.description: This year's Drink at the Creek Concert Series will once again bring you live music events in a gorgeous setting with a wide variety of performers taking the stage at Cedar Creek Winery, Brew Co and Distillery, just outside of Martinsville. Be sure to mark your calendar with the dates below! As always, this is an all ages music series and tickets are $15 in advance per person for each show with a season ticket option available. $20 at the gate. Kids 12 and under are free! item.title: 2026 Mid-Autumn Festival Fair — Sat Sep 26, 2:00 PM — Global & International Studies
item.description:
Hosted by CSSA@IU, our Mid-Autumn roaming fair welcomes all IU students to experience traditional Chinese festival culture. At the heart of the event are six interactive challenge stations themed around Mid-Autumn traditions. Attendees are free to wander throughout the venue, join culturally inspired mini-games at each booth, and take part in a fun stamp-collecting activity as they explore different stations. Complementing the game booths, we will have a lineup of song and dance performances themed around Mid-Autumn Festival on stage. The event creates a relaxed, immersive space for students of all backgrounds to learn about Chinese traditions and connect with one another. Participants will move freely between activity areas to experience the full atmosphere of the festival.
Hosted by: Chinese Students and Scholars Association
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12814121
Source: IU beINvolved Student Orgs

item.title: Lights for Life — Mon Sep 28, 10:45 AM — 10th and Fee At Arboretum - Table 1
item.description:
Stop by the 10th and Fee (entrance to arboretum) to help raise awareness for suicide prevention. Tuesday Sep 10 is World Suicide Prevention Day. Help us reach our goal of lighting up 1,100 luminaries to memorialize the 1,100 college students who lose their lives to suicide each year. Participation is easy: decorate a bag (or a few) with a positive message or drawing, get a scoop of sand, put a light inside, and place your bag on the edge of the sidewalk in the arboretum. At dusk we will turn on all the lights, so stop by to witness all the bags lit up or look out for pictures on our Instagram @balanceatkelley.
Hosted by: Balance at Kelley
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12810359
Source: IU beINvolved Student Orgs

item.title: Board of Park Commissioners Special Meeting: 2026 Investment Priorities Plan — Mon Sep 28, 5:30 PM — Switchyard Park Pavilion
item.description:
The Bloomington Board of Park Commissioners holds a special meeting to review the Parks and Recreation Department's proposed 2026 Investment Priorities Plan, a supplement to the 2026-2030 Parks and Recreation Master Plan. The plan covers how to invest in and maintain aging parks, playgrounds, trails, and recreation facilities.
No final action on the plan is scheduled. Public comment is part of the agenda, and an online option to review the information and submit comments is expected to open after the meeting.
Watch live on CATS TV: https://catstv.net/
Agenda: https://bloomington.in.gov/onboard/meetingFiles/17513/download Board page: https://bloomington.in.gov/boards/park-commissioners
Source: BloomingtonOnline Events

The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Wed Sep 30 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Oct 1 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: GALLERY WALK! BOUND BY NATURE — Fri Oct 2, 5:00 PM — Juniper Art Gallery
item.description:
Bound by Nature
20 Original Ornamental Insect Illustrations
by Jonathan Nash
Opening Reception:
First Friday Gallery Walk, Oct 2, 5-8:00pm
Special music by Elias Fisher, 6-7:30pm
Bound by Nature is a commissioned series of twenty original Art Nouveau-inspired illustrations created for the wedding of Erica Nadolkski and Jordan Evans.
Each poster celebrates a different insect personally selected by the bride, pairing it with native flora and elements of its natural habitat. Drawing inspiration from vintage natural history plates and the decorative compositions of the Art Nouveau movement, every illustration is framed by ornamental motifs unique to its featured species, incorporating elements from its life cycle, host plants, and surrounding ecosystem.

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Tue Oct 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Tue Oct 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Tue Oct 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment.
